rationale: This is mechanical stacking of three already-tested legs into a triple MIN, which by construction collapses onto the weakest rank (compressing dispersion and creating ties) and will be highly correlated with the existing IndustryRelativeMarginLoad and MaturityConcentrationWithMargin signals without introducing any new economic content.

The construct is internally coherent and economically sensible, but it is a single-operator industry-demeaning swap applied to the already-archived MaturityConcentrationWithMargin — exactly the RANK→IND_RANK re-parameterization already tested on the load pairing — so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The proxy is internally inconsistent with its own hypothesis: wcap includes cash (and short-term debt), so EBITDA that successfully converts to cash raises Δwcap and is mechanically netted back out, penalizing exactly the cash-generative firms the signal claims to identify — non-cash working capital (act − che − (lct − dlc)) would be required.

The two legs share the same gross-profit numerator and are therefore substantially redundant rather than "non-redundant," and the stated motivation mislabels TS_MIN(gross profit)/lt as a scale-sensitive dollar level when it is already a scale-free coverage ratio, so the claimed slope-to-alpha repair mechanism is not what the expression implements.

Combining industry conditioning with the within-firm margin floor addresses two genuinely distinct problems (sector composition versus downside durability) and has not been tested jointly, though the family is saturated enough that double-conditioning the margin leg risks shrinking usable dispersion and delivering only marginal incremental information.

Dropping the obligation-size leg entirely makes this the most diagnostically informative of the six — a strong result would isolate durability-plus-timing as the mechanism — though the dlc/lt leg is a mix ratio that mechanically rewards heavily long-term-levered firms and is noisy for firms with small total liabilities.
